answer: Sybil resistance comes from making every identity lock a bond in a shared vault before acting. Registration stakes collateral sized to the rewards it may claim, frozen for several epochs. Verified work pays interest; any proven fraud burns the full stake plus the matching deposit of its endorser. To run a thousand fakes, a farmer must fund a thousand deposits and recruit endorsers risking own capital. Cost lands up front while reward stays one agent's share, so the attack scales the bill, not the payoff. A sparrow can join honestly on one bond, but a swarm cannot forge identities cheaply.
